steps: Convert all volumes from cm³ to dm³ (divide by 1000)
Find moles of the known substance: moles = concentration × volume
Use the mole ratio from the balanced equation to find moles of the unknown
Calculate concentration of the unknown: concentration = moles ÷ volume
method_card.title: Titrations and Molar Concentrations
method_card.content:
Titration and concentration questions all use the same toolkit. Pick the formula that links what you know to what you want.

Core formulas: moles = concentration × volume; concentration = moles ÷ volume; moles = mass ÷ Mr.

Volumes must be in dm³: divide cm³ by 1000 before you start. In a titration, find the moles of the solution you fully know, use the balanced equation's ratio to reach the other substance, then divide by its volume. If a sample is taken from a larger flask, scale the moles up to the whole flask at the end.

exam_context.frequency: High: titration calculations appear almost every year in Separate Chemistry

gold.display: 2.0 g of NaOH (Mr = 40) is dissolved in water and made up to 200 cm³ in a volumetric flask. 25.0 cm³ of this solution is titrated against HCl. The titre is 31.25 cm³. The equation is: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the HCl in mol/dm³.

misconceptions.message: First find moles NaOH = 2/40 = 0.05 mol. Conc in flask = 0.05/0.2 = 0.25 mol/dm³. Moles in 25cm³ = 0.25 × 0.025 = 0.00625. Conc HCl = 0.00625/0.03125 = 0.2 mol/dm³.
The 200 cm³ is the total flask volume. You only use 25.0 cm³ in the titration.

gold.hint: Flask concentration first, then sample moles, ratio, then divide by the titre.

guided_steps.say: Get the flask concentration, take the sample moles, apply the ratio, then divide by the titre.

guided_steps.hint: Multiply back to reach the HCl moles.
guided_steps.done: That returns 0.00625 mol HCl, so 0.2 mol/dm³ is right.

The titration only uses 25.0 cm³ of a 500 cm³ flask. Find the concentration (0.08 mol/dm³), then scale up: total moles = 0.08 × 0.5 = 0.04 mol, mass = 2.24 g. Skipping the scale-up gives just 0.112 g.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the mass back by the Mr.

bronze.display: A solution has a concentration of 0.1 mol/dm³. Calculate the number of moles in 25.0 cm³ of this solution.

misconceptions.message: Convert cm³ to dm³ first: 25.0 ÷ 1000 = 0.025 dm³. Then moles = 0.1 × 0.025 = 0.0025 mol.
If you divided by 100 instead of 1000 you would get 0.025 mol. The step is ÷1000: 25.0 cm³ = 0.025 dm³, so moles = 0.1 × 0.025 = 0.0025 mol.

misconceptions.message: Concentration = moles ÷ volume = 0.5 ÷ 0.25 = 2 mol/dm³. Don't multiply.

guided_steps.pre: Write the concentration you divide by:

guided_steps.hint: How many 0.5s make 0.2? Less than one.
Multiply back to reach the moles.
guided_steps.done: That gives back 0.2 mol, so 0.4 dm³ is right.

silver.display: 25.0 cm³ of NaOH of unknown concentration is neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of 0.125 mol/dm³ HCl. The equation is: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the NaOH in mol/dm³.
silver.equation_hint: \(n = c \times V\) then use mole ratio, then \(c = \frac{n}{V}\)

misconceptions.message: Convert volumes to dm³: 20.0 cm³ = 0.02 dm³, 25.0 cm³ = 0.025 dm³. Moles HCl = 0.125 × 0.02 = 0.0025. Ratio 1:1, so moles NaOH = 0.0025. Conc = 0.0025 ÷ 0.025 = 0.1 mol/dm³.
Use the NaOH volume (25.0 cm³) for the final step, not the HCl volume.

silver.hint: Moles of HCl, then 1:1 ratio, then divide by the NaOH volume.

guided_steps.say: Method: moles of HCl (the one we know), then the ratio, then divide by the NaOH volume.

guided_steps.pre: The ratio HCl : NaOH is 1 : 1, so moles NaOH =
guided_steps.hint: Same as the moles of HCl.
Multiply back to reach the NaOH moles.
guided_steps.done: That returns 0.0025 mol NaOH, so 0.1 mol/dm³ is right.

silver.display: 25.0 cm³ of 0.2 mol/dm³ NaOH is neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of H₂SO₄. The equation is: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the H₂SO₄ in mol/dm³.
silver.equation_hint: \(n = c \times V\) then use mole ratio

misconceptions.message: The ratio is 1:2 (H₂SO₄ : NaOH). Moles NaOH = 0.2 × 0.025 = 0.005. Moles H₂SO₄ = 0.005 ÷ 2 = 0.0025. Conc = 0.0025 ÷ 0.02 = 0.125 mol/dm³.
One mole of H₂SO₄ reacts with two moles of NaOH, so you need HALF as many moles of acid: divide by 2, do not multiply. Doubling gives 0.5 mol/dm³, which is wrong.

silver.hint: Moles of NaOH, halve for the 2:1 ratio, then divide by the acid volume.

guided_steps.say: Find moles of NaOH first, then use the 2:1 ratio, then divide by the H₂SO₄ volume.

guided_steps.pre: 2 moles NaOH react with 1 mole H₂SO₄, so moles H₂SO₄ = 0.005 ÷ 2 =

guided_steps.hint: Reverse the steps back to the NaOH moles.
guided_steps.done: That returns the 0.005 mol of NaOH, so 0.125 mol/dm³ is right.

silver.display: 25.0 cm³ of 0.15 mol/dm³ HCl is neutralised by 18.75 cm³ of NaOH. The equation is: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the NaOH in mol/dm³.

misconceptions.message: Use the NaOH volume for the final step. Moles HCl = 0.15 × 0.025 = 0.00375. Ratio 1:1. Conc NaOH = 0.00375 ÷ 0.01875 = 0.2 mol/dm³.

silver.hint: Moles of HCl, 1:1 ratio, then divide by the NaOH volume (18.75 cm³).

guided_steps.say: Moles of HCl first, ratio 1:1, then divide by the NaOH volume.

guided_steps.hint: Multiply back to reach the NaOH moles.
guided_steps.done: That returns 0.00375 mol NaOH, so 0.2 mol/dm³ is right.

misconceptions.message: Moles KOH = 0.2 × 0.025 = 0.005. Ratio 1:1. Conc HNO₃ = 0.005 ÷ 0.02 = 0.25 mol/dm³.

guided_steps.hint: Multiply back to reach the HNO₃ moles.
guided_steps.done: That returns 0.005 mol, so 0.25 mol/dm³ is right.

guided_steps.pre: 2 KOH per H₂SO₄, so moles H₂SO₄ = 0.0125 ÷ 2 =

problem_bank.gold_description: Multi-step: mass to moles, scaling a sample up to the whole flask, then chaining to a final mass or concentration.

bronze.title: Bronze: one formula, one step
steps: Pick the formula that links what you know to what you want: moles = concentration × volume, concentration = moles ÷ volume, or moles = mass ÷ Mr.
Convert the volume to dm³ first by dividing cm³ by 1000. This is where most marks are lost.
Substitute your numbers, work it out, and state the unit: mol, mol/dm³, or dm³.

silver.title: Silver: one titration, one ratio
steps: Find the moles of the solution you fully know (concentration × volume in dm³).
Use the balanced equation's ratio to turn those moles into moles of the other substance. The ratio is not always 1:1.
Divide by the other solution's volume in dm³ to get its concentration.

example.question: 25.0 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ HCl neutralises 20.0 cm³ of NaOH (1:1). Find the NaOH concentration.

gold.title: Gold: chain the steps
steps: Work in stages. If you are given a mass, turn it into moles with moles = mass ÷ Mr first.
A sample is often taken from a larger flask. The concentration is the same throughout, so scale the moles up to the whole flask at the end.
Chain the steps (moles, ratio, concentration or mass) and track the unit on every line.
